name: Matter (plates) cannot be moved/removed at c -- massive bodies move slower than light

The theorem is instead RE-DERIVED here from its one named input, the massive dispersion relation E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4 (hypothesis H_disp), by sympy and z3 (rederive/massive-matter-subluminal.py, part A). published_statement: Not quoted at source in this stage (see source). The content the tree relies on, as re-derived here from H_disp: for m > 0 the velocity v = dE/dp = p c^2/E obeys c^2 - v^2 = m^2 c^6/E^2 > 0, so v < c for every finite momentum; v -> c only as p -> infinity, and the work (gamma - 1) m c^2 diverges as v -> c. Equivalently: the worldline of a massive body is timelike. (Restated in the docket's sibling audit from LSV gr-qc/0107091 fn 13: signal speed is c for canonical kinetic terms regardless of the sign of m^2.)
published_hypotheses: H_disp: the body's constituents obey the Lorentz-invariant dispersion E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4 with m > 0 (canonical kinetic terms; LSV fn 13 as restated by the sibling audit). Named, not read in this stage.
H_flat: special-relativistic (locally Minkowski) kinematics; in GR the statement is local -- a massive worldline is timelike, i.e. v < c relative to a local observer at the same event.

H_scope: the theorem bounds the speed of each massive element. It says nothing about how far an element must move to achieve a given physical effect; any time bound it yields is t > l/c with l the required displacement.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- the displacement/geometry factor. candidates.py:80-82 and 448-450 go from 'mechanical and therefore slower than c' to 'DEADLINE: FAILS' against 'switches off in ~R/c' (candidates.py:23, 320). The theorem gives only t_clear > l/c, where l is the displacement needed. The failure follows when l ~ R: the tree's own magnitude geometry sets the gap equal to the region size (candidates.py:118, 144, 388-392 evaluate the Casimir law at d = R), and there opening the gap R -> 2R (|rho| down 16x) takes t > R/c for every v < c (rederive part C). It does not follow when l << R: plate pairs of gap d = 1 nm and tile width w = 100 nm filling R = 1 m, each top tile sliding w off its partner at v = 100 m/s (v/c = 3.3e-7), clear in t = w/v = 1.0e-9 s < R/c = 3.34e-9 s (rederive part D; the required speed is v > w c/R = 30 m/s).

ADDED -- 'by a lot' (candidates.py:81). The theorem supplies only v < c. In the d = R geometry the deadline is missed by the factor c/v, which is 2 at v = 0.5c: '~R/c' is not failed 'by a lot' unless v << c. v << c for macroscopic plates is a DATUM (achievable mechanical speeds and accelerations), and the tree cites none. It is very likely true in practice, but it is not the theorem.

ADDED -- 'Switching it off means MOVING THE PLATES' (candidates.py:80, 449). This is an extra hypothesis: that the only switch is the plates' mechanical displacement. The Casimir interaction has reportedly been changed without moving the plates -- optical carrier-density modulation of a Si membrane (Chen, Klimchitskaya, Mostepanenko, Mohideen, quant-ph/0610094 and 0707.4390, 2007) and an effective moving boundary in a SQUID-terminated line at a few percent of c (Wilson et al. 1105.4714, 2011). All of these are NAMED-NOT-READ: they were located by web search only, and their content here is the search tool's summary. Stated with its limits: the Lifshitz energy between dielectrics is not zero, so an optical switch MODULATES and does not remove; and the 2011 device is a 1D circuit analogue. This drift is therefore recorded as unverified and is not load-bearing for the grade.

SEPARATE GROUND, NOT THIS THEOREM -- 'anchored to the plates, whose own mass-energy is hugely positive and does not go anywhere' (candidates.py:83-84). That rests on positivity and conservation of the plates' rest energy, not on subluminality. Moving that positive mass out of a region of size R does take more than ~R/(2c) by this theorem. Scope note: teardown.py:119-128 defines the deadline for the LEAD, meaning the negative-energy element, and leftover positive-mass plates are not that element. Whether the plates' presence matters to closure is the tree's own question, and it is not adjudicated here.

INTERNAL, CARRIED -- the ~R/c deadline itself (teardown.py:84, 102-107) is labelled there 'a CAUSAL-WINDOW SCALING ARGUMENT, not a theorem' with a geometry-dependent factor. So 'fails ~R/c' at an O(1) factor, which is all the theorem gives in the d = R geometry, is within that argument's own stated slack.

NOT DRIFT -- 'There is no configuration of matter that clears itself at c' (candidates.py:81-82) means self-termination without work. It agrees with teardown.py:47-56, 202-214 (matter_self_terminates False; matter_can_be_made_transient True) and is consistent with the theorem.

rederivation.outcome: Exit 0; all checks pass. (A) sympy: dE/dp = p c^2/E; c^2 - v^2 = m^2 c^6/E^2; v -> c only as p -> oo; (gamma-1) m c^2 -> oo as v -> c-; m = 0 gives v = c. z3: {m>0, c>0, E^2 = p^2c^2 + m^2c^4, E>0, v >= c} is UNSAT, and the vacuity guard (m = 0) is SAT. So the theorem is re-derived from H_disp. (B) The time bound it yields is t > l/c in the displacement l; R does not appear in it. (C) In the tree's d = R geometry, a 16-fold reduction needs a displacement of R, so t > R/c for every v < c: the qualitative DEADLINE failure follows, by the factor c/v (2 at 0.5c, 3.0e5 at 1 km/s). (D) In a microstructured geometry (d = 1 nm, w = 100 nm, R = 1 m, v = 100 m/s), t = 1.0e-9 s < R/c = 3.34e-9 s: subluminal plates meet ~R/c and the deadline failure does not follow. MAGNITUDE there still fails by 2.798e34 (34.4 orders). Caveats of (D), not modelled: PFA with edge corrections of order d/w = 1e-2; the residual pair-to-pair interaction at pitch D >> d; the ideal-plate law at 1 nm, which the tree also uses (candidates.py:542) and which real metals violate below their plasma wavelength; actuation stress, about 1 GPa for a 100 nm gold tile accelerated to 100 m/s over 10 nm, which is material-limited but not forbidden by SR; and distributing the trigger across R at c, which costs about R/c, the same as any lead.

later_literature.what: Per web-search summary only: the Casimir force between an Au sphere and a Si membrane was changed by 514 nm laser pulses (5 ms) that altered the carrier density, with no mechanical switching. If read, this narrows the tree's added hypothesis 'switching = moving plates'. It does not show switch-off, because the Lifshitz energy of a dielectric is nonzero.

later_literature.what: Per web-search summary only: a SQUID-modulated boundary condition acts as a mirror with an effective velocity of a few to about 10 percent of c. A boundary moves without massive matter moving, so the subluminal bound on plates does not bound the boundary condition. It is a 1D circuit analogue, not 3D plates.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. The theorem, that massive bodies move slower than c, depends on no measured datum. It follows from the massive dispersion relation, and c is exact by definition, so no later measurement moves it. The one empirical test that could, a Lorentz-violating dispersion of ordinary matter, was not readable in this stage and is not claimed either way. Evidence against 'the old physics was wrong' HERE: the re-derivation holds, with z3 UNSAT and a SAT vacuity guard. What the TREE lacked is not a datum the physicists lacked: it is a geometric step and an engineering datum. The step from 'v < c' to 'fails ~R/c' needs (i) the displacement to be comparable to R and (ii) v << c for 'by a lot'. The tree supplies (i) only through its own d = R magnitude geometry and supplies (ii) not at all. Supplying them changes the conclusion only in part: the DEADLINE gate is geometry-dependent (met by 100 m/s plates in the microstructured example), while the Casimir candidate still fails, on MAGNITUDE, by 34 orders at R = 1 m. The 2007 optical-modulation and 2011 effective-mirror results, if read, would weaken the tree's added hypothesis that switching means moving mass. They are recorded as unread and are not used for the grade.
grade_evidence: The theorem STANDS: it was re-derived by sympy and machine-checked by z3 (v >= c is UNSAT for m > 0, and the vacuity guard is SAT). Its use at candidates.py:80-84, 448-450 is broader than the theorem. The theorem gives t_clear > l/c for the required displacement l. The tree's DEADLINE failure follows only in the class l ~ R, which is its own d = R magnitude geometry (candidates.py:144, 388-392; rederive C), and even there the margin is c/v, so 'by a lot' is an uncited datum. In the microstructured class it does not follow: d = 1 nm, w = 100 nm, R = 1 m, v = 100 m/s gives t = 1.0e-9 s < R/c = 3.34e-9 s (rederive D). This is not WRONG: the Casimir candidate fails MAGNITUDE in both classes (34.4 orders at R = 1 m, 1 nm gap), so the candidate's overall FAIL verdict is untouched. What is geometry-dependent is first_gate_failed('Casimir') == DEADLINE (candidates.py:543). The optical and SQUID switching literature is NAMED-NOT-READ and is not used for the grade. The source is NAMED-NOT-READ in this stage (alphaXiv quota exceeded; arXiv egress-blocked), but the grade rests on the closed-form re-derivation and the computed geometry, not on a reading.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restricting the Casimir lead to the single-gap d ~ R geometry it already uses for MAGNITUDE (candidates.py:144) and citing an achievable-plate-speed datum for 'by a lot', or a proof that clearing a Casimir negative-energy region of size R needs a displacement of order R in every geometry (the microstructured example above says it does not, within PFA). To OPEN on the reading side: if a reading of the LSV restatement or an SR text contradicted H_disp as the operative hypothesis, which is not expected. Reading 0610094 / 0707.4390 / 1105.4714 at source could strengthen the drift on 'switching = moving plates', but would not change the grade class. Nothing found would move it to WRONG: the Casimir candidate's FAIL stands on MAGNITUDE.
